summary:
Australia treats gender identity as a protected ground under the federal Sex Discrimination Act, in force since 2013. In August 2024 the Federal Court held in Tickle v Giggle that gender-identity discrimination protection extends to trans women as women, and awarded compensation against a female-only dating app that had excluded a trans woman member. Visitors in every state, Western Australia included, stand under that national framework, and marriage and federal documents are uniform nationwide.

State protection in Western Australia runs through a narrower formulation. The Equal Opportunity Act 1984 protects the attribute 'gender history', defined by living, or seeking to live, as a member of the opposite sex, and the official WA Government guidance states that a person has gender history where they identify as a member of the opposite sex by living or seeking to live as such. Direct discrimination, including treating a person as their former sex, and indirect discrimination are both unlawful under the Act. The binary, medically-inflected wording means a non-binary or gender-nonconforming visitor may fall outside the state-law definition and would rely on federal coverage for a state-level complaint. Western Australia has no state anti-vilification offence, civil or criminal, and no statutory charter binding public authorities.

Complaint eligibility under the state attribute has historically been tied to recognition certificates or a registry change through the Births, Deaths and Marriages framework. On 16 April 2024 Premier Roger Cook and Attorney-General John Quigley announced the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Bill 2024, which repeals the Gender Reassignment Act 2000 and abolishes the Gender Reassignment Board, described by the ministers as the only remaining board of its kind in Australia. The Board's functions move to a streamlined administrative process within the Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, and applicants are no longer required to undergo medical or surgical reassignment. A statement from a medical practitioner or psychologist certifying appropriate clinical treatment, which may include counselling, now suffices, and a 'non-binary' sex descriptor becomes available. Stricter rules apply to under-18s through parental consent or Family Court of WA permission, and the Act contains a statutory review clause after three years. The reform implements the WA Law Reform Commission's 2018 recommendations.

The registration reform reshapes the state discrimination attribute itself. The Equal Opportunity Commission's fact sheet records that the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Act 2024 amends section 4(1) of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 by deleting the definition of 'gender reassigned person' and inserting a definition tied to recognition certificates under the Gender Reassignment Act 2000 or registration of sex or gender under the amended regime. The Act also repeals the Gender Reassignment Regulations 2001, does not operate retrospectively, and commences by proclamation; once it is in force, gender history complaints must comply with the new registration requirements.

Two complaint routes exist and only one may be used. A complaint may be lodged with the WA Commissioner of Equal Opportunity under the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 within 12 months, with acknowledgment of receipt within a week and a free conciliation conference to follow, or with the Australian Human Rights Commission under the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 within 24 months, reduced to 12 months for employment matters. Choosing one route forecloses the other.

Visitors encounter none of the restrictive machinery found elsewhere in the world: there are no laws confining bathrooms or changing facilities by gender identity in Western Australia, no border friction has been reported for trans travellers, and marriage equality has held nationally since 2017, which matters to same-sex couples arriving together.

Counterweights are documented. The Tickle case grew out of organised exclusionary activism, and ANROWS research maps current and emerging threats to trans and gender diverse rights in Australia, naming organised exclusionary campaigns, disputes over access to facilities and records, and pressure to roll back existing rights, alongside systemic discrimination and harassment experienced by trans people.
tangentialFactors:
Western Australia's reform sits inside a wider state-level movement. Queensland strengthened discrimination and vilification protections for gender-diverse people in April 2024, and New South Wales passed the Equality Legislation Amendment (LGBTIQA+) Act 2024. The WA announcement also linked the registration reform to a planned new Equal Opportunity Act and a ban on conversion practices slated for 2025.

Detention is the sharpest residual risk across the country, and the practice Western Australian visitors would meet if detained is set by interstate precedent rather than by any WA instrument in this inventory. Queensland's inspection standards issued in August 2023 direct that transgender and intersex prisoners are generally admitted to facilities corresponding to their lived or experienced gender, a placement rule with a discretionary admission caveat and an exception tied to sexual reassignment surgery; oversight there passed to the Inspector of Detention Services Act 2022, fully in force from 2023, after a 2009 corrective services procedure was assessed as largely ineffective. Equivalent Western Australian detention placement standards are not covered by the sources assembled here.

The exclusionary activism behind Tickle v Giggle indicates that private and platform-level exclusion can arise even where the statute protects gender identity, and the outcome was a compensation award rather than an injunction preventing exclusion in the first place.
localsOnly:
Western Australian residents hold two administrative entitlements under the Equal Opportunity Act 1984. A complaint goes to the WA Commissioner of Equal Opportunity, must be lodged within 12 months, is acknowledged within one week, and proceeds to a free conciliation conference; the alternative federal complaint to the Australian Human Rights Commission must be lodged within 24 months, or 12 months where employment is involved, and only one of the two routes may be chosen.

Sex and gender registration is now an administrative matter. The Gender Reassignment Act 2000 and its 2001 regulations are repealed, the Gender Reassignment Board is abolished, and applicants deal directly with the Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages on production of a statement from a medical practitioner or psychologist certifying appropriate clinical treatment, which may include counselling. Medical and surgical reassignment is no longer a prerequisite, a 'non-binary' sex descriptor is available, and applications by people under 18 require parental consent or Family Court of WA permission. A three-year statutory review clause applies.

The amendment to section 4(1) of the Equal Opportunity Act replacing the 'gender reassigned person' definition is not retrospective, and substantive commencement depends on proclamation. Once proclaimed, eligibility to bring a gender history complaint is measured against the new registration requirements.

Trans-specific support organisations operating in Western Australia include TransFolk of WA and the Freedom Centre, which serves people under 26.
outOfScopeNotes:
The consolidated PDF of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (WA) hosted on the state legislation portal could not be retrieved, because the portal blocks automated fetches. The operative definitions quoted here come from the WA Government's official explainer and the Equal Opportunity Commission's fact sheet rather than from the consolidated text itself, so the current wording of section 4 and the Act's operative provisions remain unverified against the statute.

Whether the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Act 2024 has been proclaimed and is in operation is unresolved; the Equal Opportunity Commission fact sheet records commencement as still to be proclaimed, and no later source in this inventory confirms proclamation.

Whether the planned new Equal Opportunity Act and the conversion-practices ban announced for 2025 were enacted is not sourced here. So too is the absence of a state anti-vilification offence and of a statutory charter, which rest on the absence of contrary material in the assembled sources rather than on an affirmative finding.

The WA Government gender history guidance carries a publication date of 6 August 2020 and a last-updated date of 12 February 2026, and the Justice Connect resource is dated 16 April 2026; both dates postdate other material in the inventory and were taken at face value from the sources.
